explanation: This tells the same harm as fact-91969208430137726320: the MSI is fetched over HTTPS from one fixed address (DownloadAdmx.vb 3, 84-90), unpacked with msiexec and its files replace same-named files in the destination (103-111), with no hash or signature check. Only the wording of the trust-store/proxy cause differs. One harm told twice: keep one answer for the unverified package (fold the compromised trust store or proxy cause and the default-destination reach into it; the TLS 1.0/1.1 point stays in the cryptography harm) and drop the other, or make this one tell something the other does not.

Two harms written as one: msiexec launched by bare name (line 90) is a search-order hijack; fixed scratch folders not emptied before use (79-80, 89; 114 deletes only on success) is leftover contamination. The leftover part also repeats the scratch-folder-left-behind clause of fact-83661193012540000148. Split them, and tell the leftover harm once only.

Three different harms in one: unwritable sources skipped (Main.vb 625-628; the Success box does name each as 'not writable', so call it a misleading Success headline, not silent), failed comment saves ignored (612-619), and settings storage failing silently (ConfigurationStorage.vb 4-15, a lost preference, weighing lower). Separate them, each with its own severity; medium fits lost edits and comments, not the settings key.

Mixes the non-atomic delete-then-move (64-68; ownership already changed at 99) with the generic error message (123-127) and the scratch folder left behind (114 skipped on failure). The last repeats the leftovers clause in fact-08988203210777702317. Keep this harm to the partial replacement of the destination; tell the opaque error and the leftover scratch folder once each elsewhere.
